units.title: The toolchain
units.blurb: What rustc, cargo and an edition actually are, and what `cargo run` does to your file between you pressing enter and the program starting.

units.title: Bindings and mutability
units.blurb: Why `let` is not assignment, what shadowing is actually for, and why mutability is a property of the binding rather than of the type.

units.title: Types, overflow and casts
units.blurb: Fixed-width integers that panic in debug and wrap in release, why indexing demands usize, and why `as` is the one conversion that lies to you.

units.title: Expressions and blocks
units.blurb: Almost everything produces a value, which is why `if` can be assigned from — and why one stray semicolon turns a block into nothing at all.

units.title: Control flow
units.blurb: `loop` as an expression, `while let`, labelled breaks, and the shape of a `for`.

units.title: Ownership
units.blurb: One owner, one drop. What a move actually copies, what it does not, and which bug the whole rule exists to prevent.

units.title: Borrowing and references
units.blurb: Shared or unique, never both. The rule that makes data races a compile error rather than a Tuesday.

units.title: Slices and fat pointers
units.blurb: A pointer that carries its own length, why every function should take &str, and why a string cannot be indexed by a number.

units.title: Structs and methods
units.blurb: Data with a name, three ways to write one, and what &self versus self commits every caller to.

units.title: Enums and pattern matching
units.blurb: A value that is exactly one of these, and a compiler that will not let you forget one — the best refactoring property in the language.

units.title: Option
units.blurb: Absence as a value the compiler can see, the combinators that keep it from becoming a pyramid, and the two places unwrap is still the right call.

units.title: Collections
units.blurb: Vec, String, HashMap, VecDeque, BTreeMap — what each one costs, when it reallocates, and why the entry API is the best thing in the standard library.

units.title: Error handling
units.blurb: A recoverable error is a value you return; a bug is a panic. Choosing wrong is the actual mistake, and everything else follows from getting it right.

units.title: Generics
units.blurb: One function, every type, and nothing at runtime — because the duplication still happens, it just happens inside the compiler instead of in your editor.

units.title: Traits
units.blurb: A named set of behaviour a type can implement — and the two ways to call it, one free and one costing a pointer chase.

units.title: Lifetimes
units.blurb: Not how long a value lives — a claim the compiler checks. Elision, structs that borrow, and why 'a is not a duration.

units.title: Closures
units.blurb: An anonymous function plus a struct holding what it captured — which is the one fact that explains the three traits, the move keyword and why every closure has a different type.

units.title: Iterators
units.blurb: One required method buys about seventy free ones, none of which run until something asks for an element.

units.title: Smart pointers
units.blurb: Box, Rc, RefCell and Weak — each buys one exemption from the ownership rules, and each states its price on the label.

units.title: Modules and crates
units.blurb: A package holds crates, a crate is one compilation, and a module tree decides who is allowed to see what. The layer where a program stops being a file and becomes a library.

units.title: Testing and docs
units.blurb: Tests are ordinary functions with an attribute, and the examples in your documentation are compiled and run — so your docs cannot quietly rot.

units.title: Concurrency
units.blurb: The borrow rules already forbid the exact condition a data race needs. Threads add no new rule — only the types that carry the old one across a thread boundary.

units.title: Async
units.blurb: A future is inert. Nothing runs until something polls it — which is the one sentence that explains async Rust, and the one thing a JavaScript promise does not do.

units.title: Unsafe
units.blurb: Five extra operations and a transfer of responsibility. Not an escape hatch, and not a way to switch the borrow checker off.

units.title: Macros
units.blurb: Code that runs on syntax before the types exist, which is why it can do three things a function cannot — and why it is almost never the right answer.

units.title: Reading the compiler
units.blurb: Every other unit teaches a topic. This one teaches the skill that makes the next error survivable, including the ones this book never covers.

units.title: Ship it
units.blurb: A file-searching tool from `cargo new` to a stripped release binary — the library split, clap, anyhow, two output streams, and what actually makes it small.

units.title: No_std and embedded
units.blurb: The standard library is three libraries in a trench coat. Take away the outer one and the same language runs on a chip with 20 kB of RAM and no operating system.
